packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-02 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

Exposure statement: nothing in my prior context revealed a proposed identification or earlier reading of this leaf. One caveat arising from the supplied images themselves: the overview (image-001) also shows the facing page of the host book, which carries its own red display heading. That heading belongs to the host volume's page, not to the leaf in the tiles; I transcribe it below only as a visible feature and draw no conclusion from it about the leaf read here.

==== LAYOUT SURVEY (image-only) ====

image-001 is an overview of an opened small book photographed with the board/pastedown side at the top and the first page of the text block at the bottom (rotated 90 degrees, heading running down the right edge).
image-002, 003, 004 are native tiles of the UPPER leaf only (top, middle, bottom strips; they overlap by one to two lines).

Upper leaf (the object of the tiles) - observations
- Appears to be a parchment leaf used as a pastedown/flyleaf inside the cover; text upright; one wide block in long lines (no columns visible); 20 lines visible, the last partly swallowed by the fold/gutter at the foot. The text begins mid-sentence at line 1 and runs off at the foot, so the leaf is not the start or end of a text. Whether the leaf was originally wider or had a second column cannot be told from this view.
- No running title, no rubric, no coloured initials. Slightly enlarged capitals open new items (Apud, Ante, Inuenitur, Deriuatur, Citra, Nam).
- Greek words written in Greek capitals within the Latin text.
- Right margin, same or similar ink, three short index notes level with item openings: "de apud" (with a pen flourish/paraph beneath), "de ante", "de citra".
- Right margin, written vertically in a later cursive hand: two lines, tentatively "Codex monasterij s(an)c(t)i maxi[..]i[.]?" / "p(ro)pe treuerensem? ciuitatem?" (low confidence; read from the tile edges only).
- Faint pencil number near the top right corner (looks like "24" with a stroke); small cross "+" above line 1 at left.
- Small holes and brown spots at the top; no underlining.

Lower page in image-001 (host book; NOT tiled, read from the overview only, low resolution)
- Rotated; red display capitals in two lines: "IN NOMINE D(OMI)NI IH(ES)U XP(IST)I INCIPIT PROLOG(US) / S(AN)C(T)I HIERONIMI PRESBITERI SUP(ER) MATHEUM?"; large initial P; text beginning "Plures fuisse ..."; later shelfmark-like marks and a red stamp. Not otherwise read. No native tile was supplied for it.

Tentative interpretation: the upper leaf is a list-and-discussion of individual words taken in turn (each word named, its meaning, a Greek equivalent, examples including a quoted verse), with marginal finding-notes "de X". I do not identify the work.

Areas selected: the whole upper leaf (all 20 lines) and its marginalia. Unread: most of line 20 (in the fold), the vertical later note beyond the tentative reading above, and the host-book page. A tile of the right margin at full height and an image with the fold opened would settle these.

Conventions: (..) = my expansion; [..] = unreadable; ? = uncertain; "&" kept where the scribe uses the ligature inside a word. Greek is given in the letters as written.

==== UPPER LEAF, MAIN TEXT ====

image-002
 1  satiuo iungunt(ur) · secundu(m) plerosq(ue) artium scriptores · hae apud ·
 2  ante · citra · circum · circa · erga · contra · extra · inter · intra ·
 3  infra · iuxta · prope · p(ro)pt(er) · pone ultra · praeter · supra · usq(ue) · pe
 4  nes ·, Apud · unam · hab& significationem in loco · ut apud numan
    [right margin level with line 4: "de apud"]

image-003 (lines 1-2 repeat image-002 lines 3-4)
 3  tiam adiungit(ur) tamen &iam p(er)sonis · ut apud amicum apud ethe
 4  nienses & significat · ΠΑΡΑ grecum quando locum apud illos de
 5  monstrat · ea autem p(rae)positio in conpositione non inuenit(ur) ·, Ante ·
    [right margin level with line 5: "de ante"]
 6  & conponit(ur) & separat(ur) · Antepono · ante domum & significat · ΠΡΟ
 7  graecam localem uel temporalem · ut ante eo · ΠΡΟΠΡΕΥΟΜΑΙ
 8  ante annum · ΠΡΟΕΗΙΑΥΤΟΥ ·, Inuenit(ur) &iam sine casu in quo loco
 9  aduerbii accipit(ur) significat enim antea quod est apud graecos
10  ΠΡΟΤΕΡΟΝ · Ut uergilius in bucolico · ante pererratis ambor(um)
11  [cropped at tile edge; = image-004 line 3]

image-004 (line 1 is a cropped repeat of image-003 line 9; line 2 repeats image-003 line 10)
 3  finib(us) exul · aut ararim partus bibat aut germania tigrim ·;·
 4  Deriuat(ur) ex hoc nomen antiquus · & hec antiqua & antiquu(m) · ex
 5  quo antiquarius ·, Citra numquam conponit(ur) & paene eandem
    [right margin level with line 5: "de citra"]
 6  hab& significationem · qua(m) cis ·, Nam apud nos locum significat ·
 7  sed inuenio quod propriis nominib(us) · fluminum uel montiu(m) · cis ·
 8  sol& p(rae)poni pleru(m)q(ue) · reliquis uero magis · citra · ut cis rhenum cis
 9  alpis · cis padum ·, Citra saniem · citra cruorem · citra forum · &
10  a cis? quidem? deriuat(ur)? · citra · [.....]? uero citer citerior & citim[..]
    (line 10 is half hidden in the fold; only the tops of the letters show)

Notes on particular readings
- Line 1 "satiuo": the leaf starts in the middle of a word; I give only what is on the leaf.
- image-003 line 7: the Greek after "ante eo" is written ΠΡΟΠΡΕΥΟΜΑΙ as far as I can see (one Π then ΠΡΕΥΟΜΑΙ); I have not normalised it.
- image-003 line 8: the Greek reads ΠΡΟΕΗΙΑΥΤΟΥ / ΠΡΟΕΝΙΑΥΤΟΥ (third-from-fifth letter H or N, forms are close in this hand).
- image-003 line 10: first letter of the Greek word is Π; "ΠΡΟΤΕΡΟΝ" with the final letter N-shaped.
- image-004 line 4: "hec" (written "hec"/"hęc") before "antiqua".
- Punctuation ".," / ";" marks the end of each item before the next enlarged capital.

==== MARGINALIA (kept separate) ====
- "de apud" (image-002 line 4 / image-003 line 2 level), followed below by a pen flourish resembling a large paraph or monogram.
- "de ante" (image-003 line 5 level).
- "de citra" (image-004 line 5 level).
- Vertical later note (image-003 and image-004 right edge), two lines, tentative: "Codex monasterij s(an)c(t)i maxi[..]?" and "p(ro)pe treuerensem? ciuitatem?". This is an ownership-style note in a different, later hand; I report it only as letters seen and it is low confidence.

==== LIMITATIONS ====
- Last line largely lost in the fold; nothing below it is visible.
- The start of the text is not on this face (line 1 begins mid-word); the reverse of the leaf is not shown.
- The host-book page is seen only in the reduced overview; its heading is quoted from that low-resolution view.
- This is an unverified image reading.

Reader activity: opened PROMPT.md; image-001.jpg, image-002.jpg, image-003.jpg, image-004.jpg. (READER.md and the single ls of the three assigned packet directories are recorded in the packet-01 response.) No packet.json opened.
